falsifier: A post-recolor permutation that moves a relocated atom onto a target word carrying a different symbol/type, or drops/creates a relocation, and is nonetheless accepted by apply_patch; or a build in which an existing WebFrank rule stops replaying under this change (STRICT/EQUIVALENT split moves from 56.45/9.77). Evidence lives in tools/gdl/tests/test_webfrank.py ApplyPatchObjectTests and the full ninja main.dol: OK gate.
subject: function:DrawPsysSub
value: The post_recolor_permutation stage now accepts a window carrying relocations. Its soundness rests ENTIRELY on binding each moved relocation against the target object's own relocations, word by word (name+type+word-position, EMB_SDA21 word+2 vs word+0 normalised), via the SAME verify_relocation_binding the pre-recolor instruction_permutation stage carries. The stage MUST run that binding (permute_instruction_atoms is called with our_symbols and target_relocations non-None) for every relocated window, and MUST physically rewrite the relocation table so the emitted object's entries move with their atoms. It is fail-closed: a relocation-free window reduces to the prior relocation-free path unchanged; a relocation present in the target but not ours, an exchange among same-shaped SDA atoms, or a type/symbol mismatch each raises. This widens WINDOW ELIGIBILITY of an existing stage and stays inside the class ceiling (allocator/schedule variance under the proven compiler); it is NOT a new semantic class. Measured scope of demand: DrawPsysSub is the ONLY corpus record whose structured residual.capability_needed names this capability (every other match is incidental prose), and DrawPsysSub is necessary-but-not-sufficient (its schedule window also carries the +8 frame-base immediate delta, out of ceiling), so no shipped rule exercises this path yet — the capability is proven only by the ELF fixture end-to-end tests.
